audit_kind: read-only actual-call-path audit before first independent-process acceptance
overall: Partial shared-service routing established; native/QS/output tests pass. Full common-runtime/primitive-routing and performance equivalence are not yet established.

core.behavior: Protocol::run uses the extracted original Context event loop and serialized handler/condition fixed point. Real Aptos payloads/QCs/BLS types, original native QS optimistic/certified policy and reputation tracker are used. Metadata-only commit hook adds full block digest and initial-proof flag at the two original commit pushes. Malformed signer/tag index and length checks change native panic to error; valid certificate bytes/quorum policy remain native.

network.behavior: ConsensusInbox/NativeSender and QS NetworkTransport both route bytes through shared/network-async and shared/network TCP. The outer profile is Ed25519-authenticated raptr-native-bcs-v1, distinct from Aptos transport; inner native BCS/proof bytes are unchanged. Receives retain raw-byte leases through native verification. Outbound completion means queue/defer acceptance, never waiting for a per-frame ACK; the common writer has a pipelined64-frame/8MiB window. Repair fetch traffic is classified on both native channels; initial QS transaction BCS spans are payload bytes. Self-delivery is bounded and has zeroTCP bytes.

limits.boundary: actual successful application TCP writes including owned auth/framing/ACK bytes; excludes kernel TCP/IP headers/retransmit bytes

crypto.behavior: Core BLS sign/verify/aggregate, block hash and runtime materializer BatchPayload hash route shared/crypto-aptos. QS peer Batch/SignedBatchInfo/Proof verification, proof aggregation, custody signing and NotFound signature verification are enclosed in shared operation scopes; native cache/quorum/sub-verification remains native. A repaired Batch is verified exactly once by QS NetworkSender, not both transport and QS wrapper. encode/decode preserve pinnedBCS but have no operation timer. Scope timers are nested and CPU uses calling-thread CPU, not total processCPU.

unrouted: QS BatchGenerator::create_new_batch -> Batch::new -> native cached payload.hash()/num_bytes; native_construction wrapper currently unused there.

Native transaction committed_hash used by workload TransactionSummary; application signature authentication and compatibility internals contain native primitives, some enclosed but not every internal hash separately metered.
limits.nonclaim: No claim of complete primitive call counts or summable CPU components. Offline archive verification deliberately recomputes native BatchPayload hash directly as an independent oracle and is outside runtime timing.

storage.behavior: The real typed QuorumStoreDB retains quorumstoreDB, batch and batch_ID, full digest keys, nativeBCS values, epoch cleanup and atomicdelete policy. All physicalget/put/delete/batch/scan calls route shared/store-rocksdb. Profile blob-lz4-pipelined-v1 preserves native options and Written sync=false with WAL enabled. No in-memory fallback and no Durable/power-loss barrier.

limits.warning: Requested DB-level and CF options are distinct, not a measured resident-memory/thread allocation. Native recovery loads typed maps; shared scan itself streams. Physical disk traffic/compaction costs are not measured by crypto counters.

timers.behavior: Core uses original LocalTimerService: BTreeMap<tokio::Instant,event>, last insertion wins exact deadline collision, no cancellation ID; tick removes earliest only after sleep completes. Original Context select keeps network/timer/module selection. QS retains native Tokio polling and retry timers. Shared runtime provides monotonic observer clock but does not yet own these timer queues.

workload_and_pool.behavior: shared_mempool::Worker runs arrivals on a separate OS thread, bounded sync_channel and try_send. The finite adapter owns signed native Script transactions, a capacity-limited BTreeMap<TransactionSummary,SignedTransaction>, native GetBatchRequest byte/count/exclusion handling and native commit/reject removal. This is a consensus-only finite pool adapter, not full Aptos mempool/VM validation. Native QS retains batching/custody policy.

limits.known_scope: Prepared finite transactions and rows are retained; not a constant-memory unbounded client implementation. Own batch-ready timestamp remains unavailable.

output.behavior: Native commit order synchronously reserves proof-first/original-index sections before unordered real fetch completion. Actual returned subblock-first/proofs-last native vectors are split and fully BatchPayload-verified before FIFO release. Unknown/repeated batches and empty section markers stay in raw output; common finite application controls useful identity credit and first-output admission eligibility. Capacity errors fail evidence instead of changing consensus. Full payload/journal population is bounded for this finite test.

limits.not_heap_guarantee: Encoded byte limits do not equal total Rust/JSON object heap usage; output metadata remains retained for the finite run.

execution_and_lifetime.behavior: Node starts Tokio2worker/32blocking-thread runtime, one shared network bridge OS thread, shared network peer writer/readers and one ingress OS thread. Core/DL owns at most100000 lifetime-registered handles; shutdown closes spawn admission atomically then aborts/reaps all, including after a panic. QS actor mailboxes use native configured count bounds and keyed policies. Native nested tokio::spawn/spawn_blocking still detach persistence/fetch tasks; Tokio max_blocking_threads bounds active threads, not its pending blocking queue. These internals are not covered by outer OwnedTasks. Process exit joins runtime but exact nested task completion is not separately evidenced.

limits.rayon: Unused Rayon imports in several copied QS modules do not prove active parallel work. Actual ValidatorVerifier::filter_invalid_signatures uses global Rayon fallback pool; it is not explicitly configured or reported. Its worker CPU is not captured by enclosing calling-thread meter.
limits.global_bound_status: No global retained-byte or all-descendant-task bound is claimed for nativeQS. Store quota and per-channel counts are different bounds.

clock_and_endpoint_boundaries.timebase: Same-host CLOCK_MONOTONIC microseconds for arm/planned/admitted/materialized/receipts; native protocol clocks and batch expiry retain native Tokio/SystemTime policies. No subtraction across remote clocks.
clock_and_endpoint_boundaries.admission: admitted_us sampled under state mutex immediately before successful nonblocking try_send; admission event installed after success before pool consumer can acquire state lock. This is a small pre-publication bracket, not post-enqueue clock.
clock_and_endpoint_boundaries.materialization: append_us sampled after native identity verification but before JSON assembly/serialization, byte-bound check and state push under lock. A second clock check disallows deadline-crossing credit. Event order is exact; timestamp brackets visibility by local JSON bookkeeping.
clock_and_endpoint_boundaries.freeze: Timer deadline is arm+measurement+drain; workload freezes after ingress stop, freeze_us sampled, then materializer and traffic/crypto snapshots are taken. Snapshots are pre-cleanup and not simultaneous. Deadline lateness is retained; crypto receipt signing and shutdown are after measured snapshot.
clock_and_endpoint_boundaries.latency_claim: Functional endpoint accounting only until the successful-publication timestamp bracket is tightened and full shared resource/compiler profiles are accepted.

profile_exclusions: No AptosVM execution/state-sync; valid signed synthetic Script envelope only.
Fixed quorum-signed genesis LedgerInfo is archived; advancing execution anchor/expiry fast-forward behavior is untested.
No performance comparison, global resource bound, complete primitive CPU total, or remote-host acceptance from these tests.

Missing-payload fault applies only at configured receiver to firstN authenticated initial Batch messages; consensus/custody/repair policy untouched. Fault mode adds native byte verification for drop receipts; received repair telemetry is not a standalone proof of validation.
Full/compact observer overhead comparison is not part of this finite shared-node acceptance.

next_bounded_patch_scope.method: Wrap the unchanged Batch::new call in native_construction; replace direct DB BCS encode/decode entry points with shared provider functions preserving exact errors/bytes. Retain independent native hash/BCS oracle tests.

Copy exact native BTreeMap deadline insertion/overwrite/earliest-removal/cancelled tick semantics into generic shared async timer mechanism; trait facade only in node. Keep Context select/handler atomicity and all native duration policies unchanged. Test equal deadlines and cancellation before replacing factory constructor.

Initialize one explicit Rayon2 worker pool through shared service and declare actual profile; retain original fallback verification. Enumerate OS bridge/readers/writers and native RocksDB requested workers separately. Do not sum enclosing thread CPU as workerCPU.

Inject cloneable shared spawn executor at existing spawn sites. Preserve detach-until-epoch-end and task bodies, native callbacks and persistence acknowledgment order. Register async/blocking descendant handles; explicit resource-envelope failure rather than silent drop; close spawn admission and join all on shutdown. A bounded registration cap is a declared rehost failure boundary, not an extra protocol vote/availability gate. Running spawn_blocking cannot be aborted; cleanup must wait or report noncompletion. No rewrite of protocol fixed point.
